Liquid crystals

Liquid crystals are made of elongated molecules, which keep a common orientation (the director) while flowing like a liquid. Here, the molecule is 5CB (4-cyano-4'-pentylbiphenyl), the classic room-temperature nematic liquid crystal, packed in two arrangements: a nematic phase, with the molecules aligned along z, and a twisted nematic cell, the arrangement of a pixel of a liquid crystal display, with the director turning in the plane of the cell from one layer to the next. The orientations are set by the rotation constraint, constrain_rotation, which keeps the angle between an axis and a vector of the molecule within a range.

Files: 5cb.pdb, and the input files nematic.inp and twisted.inp.

The molecule

5cb.pdb is 5CB with its pentyl chain in the extended (all-trans) conformation (built from its SMILES string, CCCCCc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccc(cc1)C#N, with Open Babel, and minimized with the MMFF94 force field). Atom 1 is the end of the alkyl chain, and atom 19 the nitrogen of the cyano group: the vector from atom 1 to atom 19, 15.8 Å long, is the long axis of the molecule, and it is the vector given to constrain_rotation, in its atoms (from) and to lines.

The molecules of a nematic phase are aligned along the director, but as many point one way as the other: the phase is apolar. So each arrangement has two structure blocks, one with the vector of the molecules along the director, and one with it opposite.

The numbers of molecules

The density of 5CB is 1.02 g/mL near room temperature, and its molar mass 249.35 g/mol: 0.00246 molecules per Å³. The nematic phase fills a periodic cube of 50 Å (125000 Å³) with 308 molecules, 154 in each direction. Each layer of the twisted cell is 50 × 50 × 15 Å (37500 Å³), with 92 molecules, 46 in each direction.

Nematic phase

Command line

#
# Nematic phase of 5CB (4-cyano-4'-pentylbiphenyl): the molecules aligned along z,
# half of them pointing up and half down, in a periodic cubic box
#
tolerance 2.0
output nematic.pdb

# Uncomment to write only the initial placement of the molecules to the output file,
# without packing them (to check the constraints):
# check_initial_placement

# Periodic box of 50 Å, centered at the origin: 308 molecules of 5CB, 1.02 g/mL
pbc -25. -25. -25. 25. 25. 25.

# The vector from the end of the alkyl chain (atom 1) to the nitrogen of the cyano
# group (atom 19) within 20° of +z
structure 5cb.pdb
  number 154
  constrain_rotation z 0. 20.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
end structure

# ... and within 20° of -z
structure 5cb.pdb
  number 154
  constrain_rotation z 180. 20.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
end structure

constrain_rotation z 0. 20. keeps the vector from atom 1 to atom 19 within 20° of +z, and constrain_rotation z 180. 20. within 20° of -z. Run it with:

packmol nematic.inp

It packs in a few seconds. The cone of 20° sets the order of the phase: the nematic order parameter, $S = \langle 3\cos^2\theta - 1 \rangle / 2$ ($\theta$ the angle of a molecule with the director), is 0.89 in the packed system, while 5CB has about 0.6 near room temperature: a cone of 45° gives 0.59.

Julia

using Packmol, PDBTools# The vector from atom 1 (end of the chain) to atom 19 (cyano N) within 20° of +z and -zup = structure_type("5cb.pdb"; number = 154,    constrain_rotation = Dict(:z => (0.0, 20.0, [1], [19])),)down = structure_type("5cb.pdb"; number = 154,    constrain_rotation = Dict(:z => (180.0, 20.0, [1], [19])),)nematic = PackmolSystem([up, down];    output = "nematic.pdb",    tolerance = 2.0,    unitcell = [50. 0. 0.; 0. 50. 0.; 0. 0. 50.], # centered at the origin    # check_initial_placement = true,)packmol(nematic)nematic.status
:packing_ready

The packed system, with the visualize function of PDBTools.jl (drag to rotate, scroll to zoom), the molecules pointing up in red and those pointing down in blue:

visualize(get_atoms(nematic),    "chain A" => (style = :sticks, color = "red"),    "chain B" => (style = :sticks, color = "blue");    unitcell = UnitCell(nematic.unitcell),    unitcell_origin = -sum(eachcol(nematic.unitcell)) / 2,)

Twisted nematic cell

In a twisted nematic cell, the molecules lie in the plane of the cell, and the director turns by 90° from one wall of the cell to the other: from x at the bottom to y at the top. Here, the cell has four layers of 15 Å, with the director at 0°, 30°, 60° and 90° from x. The cell is periodic in x and y; along z, 10 Å of empty space above the top layer separate it from the bottom one, in the periodic image of the cell.

The direction of a molecule in a plane takes more than one angle: at 30° from x, the vector is also at 60° from y (at -30° from x, it would be at 120°), and at 90° from z. So each structure block has three rotation constraints, one for each axis: for a director at an angle φ from x, the vector is at φ from x, 90° - φ from y, and 90° from z, and the opposite one at 180° - φ, 90° + φ and 90°.

Command line

The input file twisted.inp (click to expand)
#
# Twisted nematic cell of 5CB (4-cyano-4'-pentylbiphenyl): four layers of molecules
# lying in the plane of the cell, with the director turning from x, in the bottom
# layer, to y, in the top one. Periodic in x and y; the 10 Å of empty space above the
# top layer separate it from the bottom one, in the periodic image along z.
#
tolerance 2.0
output twisted.pdb

# Uncomment to write only the initial placement of the molecules to the output file,
# without packing them (to check the constraints):
# check_initial_placement

# Periodic box of 50 x 50 x 70 Å, centered at the origin: layers of 15 Å from
# z = -35 to 25 Å, 92 molecules each (1.02 g/mL)
pbc -25. -25. -35. 25. 25. 35.

# Layer 1, from z = -35 to -20 Å: the director at 0° from x, in the xy plane. The
# vector from the end of the chain (atom 1) to the cyano nitrogen (atom 19) of half
# of the molecules at 0° from x, and of the other half at 180° (antiparallel)
structure 5cb.pdb
  number 46
  above plane 0. 0. 1. -35.
  below plane 0. 0. 1. -20.
  constrain_rotation x 0.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation y 90.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation z 90. 10.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
end structure
structure 5cb.pdb
  number 46
  above plane 0. 0. 1. -35.
  below plane 0. 0. 1. -20.
  constrain_rotation x 180.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation y 90.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation z 90. 10.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
end structure

# Layer 2, from z = -20 to -5 Å: the director at 30° from x, in the xy plane. The
# vector from the end of the chain (atom 1) to the cyano nitrogen (atom 19) of half
# of the molecules at 30° from x, and of the other half at 150° (antiparallel)
structure 5cb.pdb
  number 46
  above plane 0. 0. 1. -20.
  below plane 0. 0. 1. -5.
  constrain_rotation x 30.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation y 60.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation z 90. 10.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
end structure
structure 5cb.pdb
  number 46
  above plane 0. 0. 1. -20.
  below plane 0. 0. 1. -5.
  constrain_rotation x 150.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation y 120.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation z 90. 10.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
end structure

# Layer 3, from z = -5 to 10 Å: the director at 60° from x, in the xy plane. The
# vector from the end of the chain (atom 1) to the cyano nitrogen (atom 19) of half
# of the molecules at 60° from x, and of the other half at 120° (antiparallel)
structure 5cb.pdb
  number 46
  above plane 0. 0. 1. -5.
  below plane 0. 0. 1. 10.
  constrain_rotation x 60.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation y 30.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation z 90. 10.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
end structure
structure 5cb.pdb
  number 46
  above plane 0. 0. 1. -5.
  below plane 0. 0. 1. 10.
  constrain_rotation x 120.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation y 150.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation z 90. 10.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
end structure

# Layer 4, from z = 10 to 25 Å: the director at 90° from x, in the xy plane. The
# vector from the end of the chain (atom 1) to the cyano nitrogen (atom 19) of half
# of the molecules at 90° from x, and of the other half at 90° (antiparallel)
structure 5cb.pdb
  number 46
  above plane 0. 0. 1. 10.
  below plane 0. 0. 1. 25.
  constrain_rotation x 90.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation y 0.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation z 90. 10.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
end structure

  above plane 0. 0. 1. 10.
  below plane 0. 0. 1. 25.
  constrain_rotation x 90.0 15.
    atoms 1

  end constrain_rotation

  end constrain_rotation

packmol twisted.inp

It packs in about 15 seconds with 14 threads.

Julia

The same input, with the structure types of the layers built in a loop:

# The vector from atom 1 to atom 19 at angles (x, y, z) from the axes, within 15° of# the angles with x and y, and 10° of the planefunction layer(z1, z2, (ax, ay, az))    return structure_type("5cb.pdb"; number = 46,        constraints = [AbovePlane([0., 0., 1.], z1), BelowPlane([0., 0., 1.], z2)],        constrain_rotation = Dict(            :x => (ax, 15.0, [1], [19]),            :y => (ay, 15.0, [1], [19]),            :z => (az, 10.0, [1], [19]),        ),    )endstructure_types = Packmol.StructureType{3,Float64}[]for (k, φ) in enumerate((0.0, 30.0, 60.0, 90.0))    z1 = -35.0 + 15 * (k - 1)    push!(structure_types, layer(z1, z1 + 15, (φ, 90 - φ, 90.0)))    push!(structure_types, layer(z1, z1 + 15, (180 - φ, 90 + φ, 90.0)))endtwisted = PackmolSystem(structure_types;    output = "twisted.pdb",    tolerance = 2.0,    unitcell = [50. 0. 0.; 0. 50. 0.; 0. 0. 70.], # centered at the origin)packmol(twisted)twisted.status
:packing_ready

The layers, from the bottom to the top, in red, orange, green and blue (each structure type is written with a chain identifier of its own, from A to H): seen from above, the director turns from one layer to the next.

visualize(get_atoms(twisted),    "chain A or chain B" => (style = :sticks, color = "red"),    "chain C or chain D" => (style = :sticks, color = "orange"),    "chain E or chain F" => (style = :sticks, color = "green"),    "chain G or chain H" => (style = :sticks, color = "blue");    unitcell = UnitCell(twisted.unitcell),    unitcell_origin = -sum(eachcol(twisted.unitcell)) / 2,)

get_atoms(packmol_system::PackmolSystem)

Returns the atoms of the packed system, with their current coordinates.

PackmolSystem(structure_types::Vector{<:StructureType}; output::String, kargs...)

Build a PackmolSystem directly from a vector of StructureTypes (see structure_type), without going through an input file.

packmol(input_file::String; kargs...) packmol(packmol_system::PackmolSystem; kargs...) packmol( system::SolutionBoxUS; output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., ) packmol( system::SolutionBoxUSC; concentration::Number, concentration_units::Union{Nothing,String} = nothing, output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., ) packmol( system::SolutionBoxUWI; ionic_concentration::Number=0.15u"mol/L", output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., ) packmol( system::Membrane; output="membrane.pdb", kwargs..., )

Read a Packmol input file, run the packing optimization, and write the output.

structure_type(filename; number, constraints=Constraint[], tolerance=2.0, radius=nothing, fixed=nothing, center=:none, residue_numbering=-1, D=3, T=Float64)

Build a StructureType for number copies of the molecule read from the PDB file filename, without going through an input file.

packmol( system::Membrane; output="membrane.pdb", kwargs..., )

Builds and packs a lipid membrane system, without writing an input file.

packmol( system::SolutionBoxUSC; concentration::Number, concentration_units::Union{Nothing,String} = nothing, output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., )

Builds and packs a Solute + Solvent + Cossolvent system, without writing an input file.

packmol( system::SolutionBoxUS; output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., )

Builds and packs a Solute + Solvent system, without writing an input file.

packmol( system::SolutionBoxUWI; ionic_concentration::Number=0.15u"mol/L", output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., )

Builds and packs a Solute + Water + Ions system, without writing an input file.
